claim.quote: For proton decay into the fully visible final states µ+ K0s and e+ K0s , zero and one event candidates are observed respectively. The lifetime lower limits (τ /B) thus implied are 1.5 × 1032 years and 1.2 × 1032 years, respectively.

date.note: arXiv v1 date; published Phys. Rev. D 61, 072004 (2000) per the DOI on the arXiv record.

key_value_text.value: Lifetime lower limits (tau/B) of 1.5e32 years (p to mu+ K0s) and 1.2e32 years (p to e+ K0s), zero and one candidate; 5.52 kt-yr total (4.41 kt-yr fiducial) exposure

name: Search for nucleon decay into lepton + K0 final states using Soudan 2

summary.plain: Soudan 2 looked for a proton or neutron decaying into a lepton plus a kaon. It found zero candidates in one mode and one in the other, so a proton in iron lives for more than 10^32 years in those modes.
summary.technical: 5.52 kt-yr total (4.41 kt-yr fiducial) exposure of the 963 t calorimeter: zero (mu+ K0s) and one (e+ K0s) candidate; lifetime lower limits tau/B > 1.5e32 and 1.2e32 yr; limits also for l+ K0l and n to nu K0s.

title: Search for nucleon decay into lepton + K0 final states using Soudan 2
why_it_matters: The paper notes that final states with strange mesons are expected in supersymmetric grand unified models, with predicted lifetimes of about 10^31 to 10^32 years; these limits reach that range.
